title: Kyle Howard pleads guilty to murder of wife Keeley Aspinall in Rochdale
excerpt: Kyle Howard, 37, of Tweedale Street, Rochdale, admitted murdering his wife Keeley Aspinall, 44, at Manchester Crown Court and will be sentenced on Wednesday 18 November.
body:
Kyle Howard, 37, of Tweedale Street, Rochdale, has pleaded guilty to murdering his wife Keeley Aspinall, 44, whose body was found at their home.

Howard admitted murder at Manchester Crown Court on Monday 16 November, having previously denied the offence, Greater Manchester Police said.

According to police, officers responded at about 4pm on 25 May to a report made by Howard, who said he had killed his wife at their home on Tweedale Street.

Howard told police he had stabbed Ms Aspinall two days earlier and was reporting it because her body was beginning to smell, the force said.

Officers found her body concealed under a bed, and Howard was arrested on suspicion of murder.

As paramedics attended, Howard told them: "There is no point being here, I've done it, she's dead, she's been dead for two days."

After his arrest, Howard spent several days in hospital being treated for an infection to his hand. He was discharged back into police custody on 1 June and charged with murder on 2 June.

Detective Inspector Neil Higginson, the senior investigating officer, said: "Keeley's family have been left devastated by her death and continue to come to terms with the loss of a loved one in the most tragic of circumstances.

"Kyle Howard violently took the life of a woman who should have been safe in her own home. He then concealed Keeley's body beneath a bed and left her there for two days before contacting emergency services."

He added: "Today's guilty plea means Howard has finally accepted responsibility for his actions and has spared Keeley's loved ones the added trauma of having to sit through a lengthy trial."

Howard will be sentenced at Manchester Crown Court on Wednesday 18 November.

Source: Greater Manchester Police press office, press release issued on 16 November 2026. Photograph: Rochdale Daily.
